newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - N. Sea steady, Dated weak.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - N. Sea steady, Dated weak.

text.p: The value of Dated Brent was expected to fall into line with the rest of the European crude market this week, but other North Sea grades were expected to stay steady or rise slightly, traders said.
In the Mediterranean, an overhang of prompt Urals cargoes are expected to depress prices there further.

Some traders saw some upside potential in gasoline-rich crudes, such as Norwegian Ekofisk and Nigerian Brass River, after gasoline staged a $1 per barrel rise versus Dated Brent in the past two weeks.

Shell Transport and Shipping Company (Stasco) effectively cornered the market in Dated Brent last week, buying eight cargoes loading in early November, but stopped buying on Friday and allowed the price of Dated to slip by over 30 cents versus November paper.

A November 10-12 cargo traded at Nov -20 cents on Friday after Stasco's last purchase at Nov +12 cents on Thursday. A second cargo was offered at the lower level and Friday saw the first cargo from the November programme clocked.
"The fact that Brent cargoes are running through the chains implies that Dated is worth November minus rather than November plus," a trader involved in the chain said.
"Brent's going to take a tumble next week," another North Sea equity holder said. "It will probably fall to around Dec +10. At that level it makes sense in the U.S."

Late Friday, contracts for difference valued Dated Brent at Dec +4 cents, and traders expected it to fall to that level in the absence of Stasco's support. Friday's trade was equivalent to Dec +15 cents.
Traders said Stasco would have to sell some of its eight cargoes back into Europe because the arbitrage to the U.S. Gulf was firmly shut, and this could depress Dated Brent further.
A fall in Dated would in turn improve refining margins, which took a hit last week from gas oil's collapse, they added.
"I think Stasco will reoptimise in other grades. Forties is looking quite clear and there is reasonable interest in Statfjord," said one.
The Mediterranean market was slower to react to the depressed margins and weak fundamentals than North Sea, and was expected to lose more ground this week, dealers said.
"The market looks heavy in the first decade of November.
"Also refining margins have come off with the collapse in products so I don't see great buying interest for Urals," a Rome-based trader said.
"I think the market will come off 15 or 20 cents. I wouldn't be surprised by Dated Brent -80 cents at the end of next week."
Nigerian crude has proved to be the most resilient market in the face of falling margins, but even these premiums are off their highs.
